decisions.value: Teach that before writing, the first archive was a living body — and everything it kept died with it, uncopied.

Before writing, information lived in living bodies, in two ways: in the body itself — a pattern like a spotted coat, copied into the young — and in behaviour — what the young learned by watching. If it was not passed on, it died with the body. (Essence: 'Life stored information in bodies first.')
The Earth One lane-standard audience: a general cold viewer addressed at high-school plain language. The misconception the piece corrects (S-01): 'information needs writing / records are human-made.'

Earth One Episode 1 — the INTRODUCE step of the Planet's Story (playlist 'The Planet's Story — Observations', Earth One channel): the opener of the information-evolution arc every later episode continues. It installs the series' premise (information has homes; the first was alive) and its engine (that home could die), and its ending routes the viewer onward to Ep.2.

Five moves, prescribed from the objective: M1 THE OPEN QUESTION (writing's youth stated; the question asked; the invite; the think beat — the world holds its breath) → M2 THE ANSWER IS A BODY (the claim lands on living bodies: three generations standing in a line — the archive shown before it is analysed) → M3 TWO DOORS (the pair declared, then proved one door at a time: the coat that hides from the lion, performed; the route to water, drawn and followed) → M4 THE FATAL RULE (scale first — copy after copy for millions of years — then the turn: die uncopied and everything dies with you; the sting stands alone) → M5 EPITAPH + THE DOOR OUT (the plain statement; the bookend: the first archive was a living body; then the spoken carry — the next home named, the Academy plugged in the piece's own terms). Spine: And–But–Therefore, re-derived below.

Question opening — the prediction hook, WITH its suspension built into the architecture (the #54 repair as a structural member, not a patch): L1 states writing's youth as a striking number and asks where information lived before it; L2 is the invite (a delivery-role line, the owner's own example phrase from his #54 feedback); then the F3 think beat (1,500 ms) runs with the question visibly open on screen — the empty dawn world holds, no animal yet, the question's words stay lit — before L3 answers. The expected completions (caves, memory, stories) are all wrong; the payoff reframes the question.

RECORDED EXPERIMENT — THE ILLUSTRATED WORLD, PERFORMED. Spine: Earth One's own picture-book world (format v4): full-bleed painted plates as the stage, independent cutout objects over them, hand-lettered word animation in each scene's planned negative space. The variable under test: PERFORMED TRANSFORMATIONS inside held plates — the coat's copy arrives as a new body in the grass; the route to water DRAWS ITSELF across the plate and is followed; at the fatal rule the light dies and the still body replaces the standing world; the dawn returns for the epitaph. NOT the A59 typographic void (soa-01 / wd-01 / wd-02's grammar — a definitional-lane stage; Earth One's identity is a place, and this piece's proofs are animals, not terms), and NOT whiteboard construction (ws01-v2 is already testing the blueprint register on the flagship lane; a construction register would fight this story's deep-time warmth). Delivery half of the experiment: storyteller cadence — the suspension is scenic (the world holds its breath with the question open), line transitions at the warm end of the doctrine's ranges. HYPOTHESIS: for a story-lane episode, attention rides on a world that changes in place; if the performed transformations hold the viewer better than plate succession did (the old build's H7 weakness), the lane gains its default visual mode for the next batch (the slate's own comparison plan names this unknown).

Storyteller cadence over the five moves: the suspension architecture is structural (M1's invite + F3 think beat; suspense priced before the turn; the sting isolated on its own breath; consolidation after the peak), transitions are guideposts at the joints where the thought changes kind, and every inter-line gap is priced by function from the pause doctrine's classes at phase 3 — no flat gaps anywhere (defect D5 is the anti-pattern). Intonation intent is recorded per line at phase 3 and binds the synthesis. The music bed is one continuous, level-locked track under the whole piece (lane constants, files/earthone-format.md §Music bed); pauses live in the narration only.

A SPOKEN CARRY inside the architecture (M5's second half), in two short lines after the epitaph: (1) the next home named — the story told out loud, 'the first backup' — which is Ep.2's subject and title concept, so the referral lands on a named, existing next thing; (2) the Academy plug in the piece's own terms — the story of where information lives is the story Hadosh Academy tells, and its newest home is the one you build and own yourself. Then the end card (finale world held): 'NEXT — THE STORY WAS THE FIRST BACKUP' + 'EARTH ONE'. The banned formula appears nowhere — not spoken, not on the card, and (packaging note for the future upload) not in any description this branch would ship.

ONE self-contained HTML file (the MP4 renders from this file alone), in six compartments: C0 THE WORLD — the plate layer (eight painted plates, cover-cropped, slow push-in per the lane's dialect; damaged regions routed out of frame by the crop/zoom choices recorded per plate); C1 THE ACTORS — independent cutout objects (the lion, the young antelope, the still body, trees) entering, exiting and transforming over the plates; C2 THE TRANSFORMATIONS — the performed layer (the copy arriving in the grass; the route drawing itself as a dotted line and being followed; the light dying at the fatal rule; motion itself halting at the sting); C3 THE WORDS — word animation per line in the scene's planned negative space (hand lettering; ≤3 words on screen; the key word carries the pop) — the ONLY narration text in the piece: there is no caption band, no plate element, nothing at the bottom of the frame that carries text across lines; C4 THE LABELS — one hand-lettered scene label per beat, in negative space (titles, not narration text); C5 THE CARDS + BUG — opening card (dawn plate + EARTH ONE + the title), end card (finale held + NEXT tease + EARTH ONE), the small EARTH ONE bug top-left inside the safe rect. An editor layer rides the file (click an element, adjust, copy the overrides out) — the package's editability proof at phase 7.
